lesson: CORRECTED BY DATA (see HOT_DAY_CALIBRATION.md): my same-day reaction -- 'shift PHX center up ~2F' -- was an overcorrection from 2 anecdotes. Measured on 402 hot PHX days (2015-25): median error is only +0.9F, BUT P(actual >= fc+2F) = 24% vs P(<=-2F) = 7%. So the real edge is the ASYMMETRY, not a big shift: on hot PHX days the bucket ABOVE center deserves ~24% weight, which is why the market's warm bucket keeps winning and why declining it 'on principle' was wrong. Critically this is CITY-SPECIFIC and sign-flipped: Vegas hot days run the OTHER way (median -1.0F, P(>=+2F) only 6%) and NYC is centered but wide (23%/17%). Encoded in models/hot_day_calibration.py.
